messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — rolled a small canary of v3-int4 (contrastive-tuned) to 2% traffic for long-doc. CPU/GPU tail looks great but a couple of red flags in the eval slices.

igor: what metrics are tripping? can you paste the A/B diffs?

maya: Sure. TL;DR: latency p50 down ~28%, cost-ish down ~35%. But on the long-doc slice MRR delta = -1.9% (95% CI excludes 0), hallucination-rate +1.1pp absolute on the 'citations' slice. sample sizes: control n=14k, variant n=9k.

li: sample sizes OK but variant n is smaller — what's the timeline? are these production traffic numbers or seeded traffic?

maya: production, ~1.5h window. We seeded additional long-doc tests in shadow earlier (see staging run id 2026-03-22T08:11).

igor: negative MRR >1.5% and halluc +1pp is concerning. Our current auto-fallback thresholds are -2% MRR OR halluc +2pp, but that's global. For long-doc we never set slice-specific thresholds.

sophia: suggestion: add slice-aware rules. e.g. for long-doc enforce MRR threshold -1.0% (stricter), and require at least 5k effective samples before a forced rollback. Start canary at 0.5% and ramp if pass.

zach: also add a latency tail circuit-breaker: if p95 latency increases by >150ms for 5 minutes, circuit trips and traffic routes to previous model variant. we saw regressions in cold-starts with int4 in other tenants.

maya: here's the canary config I pushed (sanitized):
```json
{"canary": {"initial_fraction": 0.02, "ramp": [0.02, 0.05, 0.2], "slices": {"long-doc": {"max_mrr_drop_pct": 1.0, "min_samples": 5000}}, "auto_fallback": {"global_mrr_pct": 2.0, "hallucination_pp": 2.0, "p95_latency_ms": 150}}}
```

igor: OK. two asks: 1) we need per-slice evaluation instrumentation in the console so operators get a bell for long-doc specifically. 2) tie the auto-fallback to an evidence window (e.g., 15m rolling with min samples) to avoid noisy spikes.

li: about the hallucination measurement — which detector was used? simple keyword match or model-based classifier? that changes the threshold sensitivity.

maya: using the model-based hallucination classifier v2 (prod detector). We also logged raw examples to S3 for quick manual audit.

sophia: can we run a paired bootstrap on the long-doc subset to validate MRR delta? this will reduce freak p-values from different traffic mixes.

maya: doing that now, results in ~10m. will post when ready.

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary v3-int4 -> 2% @ maya (1822223333)

zach: fyi, add a short-circuit for bursty traffic — hill-climb ramps only if p95 < baseline + 50ms for 10 consecutive minutes. helps with noisy cloud bursts.

maya: bootstrap done. paired CI still shows negative (median -1.85%, 90% CI [-2.4, -1.2]). Hallucination paired increase ~1.05pp (CI excludes 0).

li: sounds statistically significant. my vote: rollback to v3fp16 for long-doc traffic slices and keep int4 for short-doc routes. We can do a split-route: session-level routing by doc-length hash.

igor: +1. also open a ticket to add per-slice automatic fallback (configurable) and surface sampled failing pairs in the console for immediate triage.

maya: rolling back long-doc slice to v3fp16 now, keeping overall canary at 1% for short-doc until we run more shadow evals. will document the experiment and add notes in the canary runbook. :handshake:

zach: thanks — can we add an automated smokecheck that queries 200 long-doc items before ramping beyond 1%? small protection but high signal.

sophia: agree. we should also record the quantization kernel version in the rollout metadata (some regressions correlate with kernel rev).

maya: good call, adding that. will pin kernel rev `k8-quant-v3.4` in the next attempt.

li: assign followups? i'll own the rollback ticket and the paired bootstrap job. igor — can you add the slice fallback config to the gatebook docs?

igor: on it. I'll add an example and a recommended default threshold table.

maya: thanks team. I'll file a postmortem sketch with graphs and sample diffs in #eng-ml-postmortems later today.

sophia: :thumbsup:

zach: :rocket:
